classification.difficultyReason: Apply the explicitly taught diagonal-bisection property to two symbolic half-lengths, double both and compare their ratio; no new proof selection is demanded.

content.prompt: Show that the diagonal $AC$ in the diagram below has twice the length of the diagonal $BD$.

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD with A upper left, B upper right, C lower right and D lower left. Opposite horizontal sides have double parallel arrows; the other pair has single arrows. Red dashed diagonals meet at M. Ordinary source blue outlines and parallel marks use house black; the diagonal distinction retains standard red.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel to DC; AD parallel to BC; M is the intersection of AC and BD; AM=2x; BM=x. Drawing coordinates represent topology and are not supplied measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and labels are visible; no inferred half-diagonal lengths or conclusion are supplied.

answer.short:
$AC=2BD$.

The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so $AC=4x$ and $BD=2x$.
answer.worked:
The diagonals of parallelogram $ABCD$ bisect each other, so $MC=AM=2x$ and $MD=BM=x$.
$$\begin{align*}AC&=AM+MC\\AC&=2x+2x\\AC&=4x,\\BD&=BM+MD\\BD&=x+x\\BD&=2x.\end{align*}$$
Hence $AC=2BD$.
